title: PSU Banks Surge Up to 8% on PNB Beat as HDFC, Axis Fall Despite Profit Growth
excerpt: Punjab National Bank's 13% profit rise and margin improvement sparked a public sector rally, while narrowing margins and weak treasury income dragged HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and ICICI Bank lower despite profit growth across all three.
body:
• Public sector bank shares surged up to 8% on Monday, October 19, led by Punjab National Bank, while private lenders fell up to 5% — a split driven entirely by how investors read the September-quarter (Q2 FY27) results.
  • PNB reported standalone net profit of Rs 5,532 crore, up 13% year-on-year, with net interest income up about 11% to Rs 11,601 crore; brokerages raised target prices after the beat.
  • Axis Bank fell over 5% intraday despite a 38% profit rise to Rs 7,003 crore, because the result missed analyst estimates and its net interest margin held at just 3.36%; HDFC Bank fell over 2% on a narrower margin despite profit of Rs 19,510 crore.
  • For investors: the market rewarded margin direction, not headline profit growth — every major private lender grew profit, and all of them were sold.

India's banking stocks split sharply on Monday, October 19, as investors rewarded public sector lenders for a clean earnings beat and punished private banks whose September-quarter results, though profitable, showed narrowing margins and weaker treasury income. The Nifty PSU Bank index rose more than 2%, while the Nifty Private Bank index fell — by 1.85% at the close, according to Upstox's market wrap — and the broader Sensex dropped 876 points to close at 73,853.

PNB leads the PSU rally

Punjab National Bank set the tone. Its shares soared 8% after the lender reported a 13% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 5,532 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, with net interest income rising about 11% to Rs 11,601 crore from Rs 10,469 crore a year earlier, according to The Economic Times. Brokerages including Jefferies and Motilal Oswal raised target prices after the results beat estimates, and asset quality improved.

The strength spread across the sector. Union Bank of India gained as much as 5.5% after reporting net profit of Rs 5,537 crore, up 30% year-on-year, with net interest income jumping 20% to Rs 10,583 crore, Upstox reported. Canara Bank and Union Bank rose over 3% each in the Economic Times tally, Bank of Baroda and Bank of India rose over 2% each, and State Bank of India, Punjab & Sind Bank, Bank of Maharashtra, Indian Bank and Central Bank of India rose around 1% each.

"Union Bank of India gained as much as 5.5% after reporting net profit of Rs 5,537 crore, up 30% year-on-year, with net interest income jumping 20% to Rs 10,583 crore, Upstox reported."

Private lenders: profit up, shares down

The private banks' problem was not profit — it was what sat underneath it. Axis Bank reported a 38% year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore, with net interest income up 12% to Rs 15,371 crore. Its shares still fell over 5% intraday and closed 4.2% lower at Rs 1,236, the top loser in the Nifty 50, after the profit narrowly missed the LSEG analyst estimate of Rs 7,124 crore. Rising bond yields and rupee volatility weighed on treasury income, Reuters reported, and the bank's net interest margin was 3.36%.

HDFC Bank, India's largest private lender, fell over 2% after reporting net profit of Rs 19,510 crore, up about 4.6% year-on-year. The detail investors focused on was margin: its net interest margin eased to 3.16% on total assets from 3.30% in the June quarter, while treasury trading gains fell to about Rs 780 crore from Rs 2,390 crore a year ago, according to 5paisa's earnings analysis. Gross bad loans improved to 1.11% of advances.

ICICI Bank slipped over 1% despite the strongest headline numbers of the three: net profit up 20.1% to Rs 14,843 crore and net interest income up 17.7% to Rs 25,339 crore. Its margin still contracted — to 4.18% from 4.36% in the June quarter and 4.30% a year earlier — and it booked a Rs 230 crore treasury loss against a Rs 220 crore gain a year ago. Yes Bank fell over 1%, while Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bandhan Bank and IndusInd Bank fell nearly 1% each.

Why margins decided the day

The common thread was funding cost. Part of the squeeze traced to foreign-currency FCNR(B) deposits, which swell balance sheets but can depress reported margins while funds sit in lower-yielding assets awaiting deployment. ICICI's deposit growth was 27.1% including FCNR(B) but 17.0% excluding it; Axis disclosed a margin of 3.47% excluding the FCNR(B) impact against its reported 3.36%. Investors, in other words, were pricing the quality and direction of core lending income rather than rewarding balance-sheet growth alone.

Broader sentiment did not help. Brent crude above $108 a barrel and broad-based selling — 2,717 shares declined against 846 advancing on the NSE — left little patience for results that merely met a high bar. Goldman Sachs, by contrast, said the private banks' earnings were largely in line with expectations and that its thesis of a cyclical inflection in core pre-provision operating profit growth remains on track, Upstox reported.

What to watch

Technically, the Nifty Bank index dropped to 55,650 after two strong sessions. Vatsal Bhuva, technical analyst at LKP Securities, told the Economic Times the index has reclaimed its 20-day moving average with the RSI holding above 50, pointing to a possible move toward its 50-day average — with 56,200 as resistance and support at 55,200 and then 55,000.

The fundamental question for the coming sessions is narrower: whether PNB's margin and asset-quality improvement marks a durable PSU re-rating, and whether private lenders can show margin stabilisation next quarter. On Monday's evidence, the market has already decided which story it believes first.
